newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia cuts Clayoquot Sound tree harvest.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia cuts Clayoquot Sound tree harvest.

text.p: British Columbia said Friday that it made a sharp cut in the timber harvest on central Vancouver Island including part of controversial Clayoquot Sound.

The government said it lowered the allowable annual cut on tree farm license 54 held by International Forest Products Ltd by 45 percent to 75,750 cubic meters. It also reduced the cut for the Arrowsmith timber supply area by 14 percent to 400,000 cubic meters a year.
A small part of the Arrowsmith area and almost all of license 54 lie within Clayoquot Sound, an area of rain forest that has been a focus of environmental protests.
The government said the cuts result from its decisions in recent years to reduce logging in the sound and adopt a scientific panel's recommendations on sustainable logging.
The two areas account for 42 percent of the harvest from Clayoquot Sound. The province will rule on the remaining tree farm license 44 held by MacMillan Bloedel Ltd next year.
